messages:
elena: Hey team, hitting a weird rerank bug — all returned scores are 0 and sometimes we get a 422 when we include nested query fields inside docs. Minimal repro below, can someone confirm if this is a payload shape issue?

ben: Can you paste the request you sent (headers + body)? 422 usually means a schema mismatch.

elena: Sure — prod key redacted. Body:```json
{
  "query": "how to refund",
  "documents": [
    {"id": "d1", "text": "refund policy...", "query": "refund process"},
    {"id": "d2", "text": "billing cycles..."}
  ]
}
```

ml-eng-aaron: Ah — you have a per-document "query" field. The rerank API treats a top-level "query" as the user query; doc-level "query" is ambiguous. Depending on SDK flattening, the server may interpret documents as candidates or strip the root query. That explains zeros.

support-bot: ERROR 422: "Unexpected field 'query' inside docs. Use 'metadata' if you need doc-level annotations. Request id: req_0a1b2c3d

elena: Interesting — the SDK our client uses auto-flattens nested objects into top-level keys for legacy reasons. I can repro with curl too:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d @payload.json
```payload.json is same as above.

sam: Quick question — how many candidates/docs in your real request? If the service thinks your docs are the candidates array it can hit score normalization code paths that produce zeros when the query is missing.

elena: This is tiny — 5 docs. Not hitting any size limit.

ben: Can you try adding an explicit empty candidates array and moving per-doc annotations under "metadata" to confirm? Eg:```json
{
  "query": "how to refund",
  "candidates": [],
  "documents": [
    {"id": "d1", "text": "refund policy...", "metadata": {"note": "refund process"}},
    {"id": "d2", "text": "billing cycles..."}
  ]
}
```

elena: Tried that — got a valid response but scores were still all 0. Response snippet:```json
{
  "results": [
    {"candidate_id": "d1", "score": 0},
    {"candidate_id": "d2", "score": 0}
  ]
}
```

ml-eng-aaron: Oof. Can you share the trace id or request id for that call? Also include the server-side warning if present. We recently shipped a change: when both candidates and documents arrays exist, the runtime may choose the smaller array as the ranking set; but if the root query is missing (or overwritten by empty string), scoring returns zeros.

elena: Request id for the zero-score response is req_9f8e7d6c. No warnings in body, but we captured the header: X-Redwood-Warn: "schema_conflict: doc.query overrides root.query".

ben: Thanks. I'm going to open an eng ticket and loop in @eng-ml and @eng-runtime. Likely cause: SDK flattening + permissive schema allowed doc-level query key which overwrote root query during parsing. Short-term workaround: ensure unique key names (avoid "query" inside docs) or pass "schema_validation": true in the request to reject ambiguous shapes.

ml-eng-aaron: For repro, we can run the payload through our parser locally. Repro steps for eng: 1) Use payload above with per-doc "query" 2) Run through v2-parser binary with --flatten-sdk flag 3) Observe root query becomes empty and docs are promoted to candidates 4) Scores compute as 0. Example CLI:```bash
./v2-parser --input payload.json --flatten-sdk | jq .parsed
```

support-bot: Created support ticket SUP-2026 and incident link: https://redwood.status/s/INC-2026. Escalated to eng-runtime.

elena: Appreciate the quick triage. Action items for us: rename doc-level field to "metadata.query_hint" and enable schema_validation for now. Please keep me posted when there's a runtime fix.

ben: Will do — I've added an internal patch to reject conflicting keys and flagged for a rollback window if the fix causes client regressions. @ml-eng-aaron will follow up with timeline.

ml-eng-aaron: ETA for a fix patch is ~48 hours. We'll add stricter validation and an opt-in compatibility mode. Also adding a warning when SDK flattening patterns detected.

elena: Great, thanks everyone. I'll update the customer and roll the workaround into our client library docs.
